blocks.title: Commercial Engine
blocks.body: Design Hotels commercial distribution rides Marriott Bonvoy direct channels, GDS, OTAs, and parent sales systems. Design-led independent collection: architecture and cultural originality with Marriott Bonvoy commercial systems for owners who can sustain design QA. Owners should underwrite channel mix and loyalty contribution for this asset—not corporate averages alone.

blocks.title: Commercial Differentiator
blocks.body: Versus Autograph and Tribute soft collections, Design Hotels prioritizes design originality and member curation; underwrite design capital and standards discipline carefully.

blocks.title: Channels
blocks.body: Brand.com / Marriott Bonvoy app · major OTAs · GDS · metasearch (where active for the hotel)

blocks.title: Campaigns
blocks.body: Marriott Bonvoy and parent portfolio campaigns where the hotel is eligible

blocks.title: B2B Programs
blocks.body: Corporate, SME, and RFP programs routed through parent sales infrastructure where active for this flag

blocks.title: Owner Lens
blocks.body: Model Design Hotels contribution after loyalty chargebacks, preferred-agency commissions, and local competitive set reality—not headline RevPAR alone.

blocks.title: Distribution & Channel Mix
blocks.body: Parent central reservations, Marriott Bonvoy app, and designated online channels—confirm commission structures and rate parity obligations in the current agreement exhibit.

blocks.title: Revenue Management
blocks.body: Parent revenue tools and Marriott Bonvoy demand signals support pricing experiments; owners still need property-level strategy for this brand's product promise.

blocks.title: Digital Marketing & Performance Media
blocks.body: Paid and owned media templates at portfolio scale, with creative that must still feel brand- and hotel-specific rather than generic parent advertising.

blocks.title: Corporate, SME & Group Pull
blocks.body: Contracted travelers, small meetings, and negotiated programs where Design Hotels fits the account's brand ladder.

blocks.title: Owner Perception Risk
blocks.body: Owners sometimes expect lifestyle lightness without systems cost; Design Hotels still carries parent systems, Marriott Bonvoy economics, and brand QA. Align IC expectations early.

blocks.title: Marriott Bonvoy
blocks.body: Design Hotels participates in Marriott Bonvoy. Members earn and redeem points and receive Elite recognition across participating sister brands. Confirm current tier names and earn rules on the official program site before IC.

blocks.title: Loyalty
blocks.body: Marriott Bonvoy at Design Hotels

blocks.title: Earn
blocks.body: Guests earn Marriott Bonvoy points on qualifying stays at Design Hotels. Elite members may receive enhanced earn and recognition benefits per current program rules.

blocks.title: Redeem
blocks.body: Points redeem for stays across the Marriott Bonvoy portfolio, including Design Hotels, subject to availability and current redemption charts.

blocks.title: Elite Recognition
blocks.body: Elite status recognition (upgrades, late checkout, lounge access where offered) applies per property capability—delivery varies by hotel.

blocks.title: Ecosystem
blocks.body: Marriott Bonvoy partnerships, co-branded cards, and bonus campaigns expand the loyalty halo; Design Hotels stays remain the property-level earn/redeem node.

blocks.title: Owner Lens
blocks.body: Marriott Bonvoy drives distribution and repeat demand but adds loyalty chargebacks and program economics. Underwrite net contribution after loyalty—not membership vanity metrics.

blocks.title: P&L Implications
blocks.body: Loyalty assessments and program contribution affect net rooms revenue. Use current agreement exhibits; do not invent undisclosed rates.

blocks.title: Operating Implications
blocks.body: Front desk and systems must support Marriott Bonvoy enrollment, Elite recognition, and redemption stays without erasing the brand's guest experience.

blocks.title: Systems Implications
blocks.body: Parent property and reservation systems integration is required for Marriott Bonvoy participation—budget cutover and training in the conversion plan.

blocks.title: Repeat Guest Capture
blocks.body: Marriott Bonvoy earn and recognition increase the probability of repeat Design Hotels stays where the hotel already competes on product fit—not on a standardized prototype alone.

blocks.title: Direct Channel & Member Pricing
blocks.body: Bonvoy member rates and Marriott direct paths help Design Hotels hotels defend contribution against high-commission intermediaries while keeping brand positioning intact.

blocks.title: Elite Member Value
blocks.body: Elite recognition (upgrades where available, late checkout, milestone rewards) supports contribution at Design Hotels; amenity delivery still varies by property capability.

blocks.title: Cross-Brand Traveler Flow
blocks.body: Bonvoy recognition across Marriott sister brands matters for guests who split stays within the network—Design Hotels remains the brand-specific node inside that earn/redeem graph.

blocks.title: Cobrand & Payment Scale
blocks.body: Bonvoy co-branded cards, Moments, and bonus-point campaigns lift acquisition; model hotel-level contribution after loyalty chargebacks—not portfolio vanity metrics.

blocks.title: Corporate & Small Meetings
blocks.body: Marriott account linkage and negotiated transient patterns support midweek compression where corporate and SMERF mix fits the Design Hotels asset—confirm for this hotel's source markets.

blocks.title: To Join
blocks.body: Design Hotels affiliation / application, program fees, and Bonvoy assessments — confirm current Marriott or Design Hotels disclosure exhibits. Amounts are not staged without a verified disclosure.

blocks.title: To Operate
blocks.body: Steady-state royalty, program contribution, and Marriott Bonvoy loyalty assessments — confirm definitions, bases, and current percentages in the live disclosure exhibit for Design Hotels. Do not underwrite from peer rumor.

blocks.title: When Things Change
blocks.body: Renewal PIP; conversion PIP revisions; transfer / change-of-ownership fees; termination-related obligations; owner-funded reserves—triggered at renewal, repositioning, or exit. Confirm liquidated damages and transfer mechanics in the current agreement.

blocks.title: Fee Variability
blocks.body: Initial vs conversion paths differ; program contribution and loyalty assessments may change by year under agreement terms. Lock the fee exhibit before IC—never extrapolate from a peer hotel's rumor. Geography note: Confirm current Marriott / Design Hotels affiliation disclosure

blocks.title: Why Value Is Strongest in These Scenarios
blocks.body:
Keep Local Product Intent—Add Marriott Bonvoy: retain Design Hotels's brand promise while accessing loyalty earn/redeem and parent commercial systems a standalone hotel cannot buy alone.
Design-led independent collection: architecture and cultural originality with Marriott Bonvoy commercial systems for owners who can sustain design QA.
Sibling Clarity: diligence fit versus same-parent peers before assuming identical owner use case or fee path.
Operator & Owner Fit: strongest when the asset can deliver the brand's guest promise with QA discipline—weakest when sponsors want the flag without the product investment.
Disclosure Discipline: model economics only from current fee exhibits—Factory 2.0 does not invent undisclosed percentages.

blocks.title: Design-Original Independent
blocks.body: Hotels where architecture and design authorship are the product—pair Bonvoy distribution with design QA that protects originality.

blocks.title: Cultural Destination Landmarks
blocks.body: Destination assets where cultural programming and design narrative drive rate power inside the Marriott soft-collection ladder.

blocks.title: Sibling Clarity Versus Autograph
blocks.body: Assets that need diligence against Autograph and Tribute before assuming the same owner use case, fee path, or design capital stack.

blocks.title: Regional & Secondary Markets
